branch: api_retry storm — enum translated to readable text, twin-emission dedupe, per-turn reset
provenance: The api_retry frame shape and its five-code `error` enum are read VERBATIM from the 2.1.226 binary (strings on ~/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.226): `subtype:"api_retry",attempt:…,max_retries:…,retry_delay_ms:…,error_status:….status??null,error:c_r(…)` where c_r maps 529→overloaded, 429→rate_limit, 401|403→authentication_failed, ≥408→server_error, else the literal "unknown" (a network failure has no status — 9.1's storm read `unknown — retrying (n/10)` because the enum word was echoed to the screen). The DOUBLE emission is from the same binary: the raw api_error frame falls through the stream translator's `else yield` and THEN the api_retry twin is yielded for the same attempt — raw twin first. The api_error twin's {retryAttempt, maxRetries, error:{message, formatted}} spelling is the persisted-transcript shape probed 2026-08-06 (client-parity item 32). Defect observed on the 2026-08-07 pass via `nmcli networking off`: every line read 'unknown — retrying (n/10)' and '(1/10)' rendered twice.

steps.note: attempt 1 arrives TWICE (raw api_error twin first, translated api_retry twin second) — one line, the richer text wins

expect.why: 9.1(2): the twin pair draws ONE line, not two
raw twin arrives first, so its richer formatted text is the line that stays
9.1(1): the enum word never reaches the screen. Assert on #log, never document.body — body.textContent includes chat.html's own script source, which now contains these very literals

steps.note: later attempts arrive as api_retry only, error:'unknown' — translated to the TUI's own generic wording

expect.why: 9.1(1): 'unknown' resolves through RETRY_REASONS to readable wording
still never the raw enum word
three attempts, three lines — dedupe suppresses twins only, not distinct attempts

steps.note: the coded reasons translate, with the HTTP status kept in parentheses
negative control: a code RETRY_REASONS has never heard of degrades to the raw code, never to nothing

expect.why: an unfamiliar future code still surfaces (same degradation rule as AUTH_BLOCKED)

steps.note: a SECOND storm in the same turn restarts at (1/10) — last-key dedupe must not swallow it

expect.why: 6/10 was the last key, so a fresh 1/10 is a NEW retry, not a twin — a Set here would wrongly hide it

steps.note: per-turn reset: after a clear, the same attempt key renders again

expect.why: retrySeen resets with the session — a stale key from the old conversation must not suppress the new one's first retry
